sources: University of Maine Cooperative Extension, Giant Water Bug (Lethocerus americanus) fact sheet: 2 to 4 inches long, the largest true bug (Hemiptera) in the US and Canada; common names include toe-biters (they can inflict a painful bite) and electric-light bugs (adults fly and are attracted to lights at night); https://extension.umaine.edu/home-and-garden-ipm/fact-sheets/common-name-listing/giant-water-bug/

KQED Science / Deep Look (PBS), Don't Go Chasing Water Bugs, quoting entomologists Chris Goforth (North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences) and Robert Sites (University of Missouri): bite among the most painful of any insect, delivered with dagger-like mouthparts; they inject venom that liquefies the prey's insides and suck it back out, the prey likely still alive; they eat animals as large as turtles, snakes and ducklings; in Abedus the female glues eggs onto the male's back and leaves, and he carries them for several weeks; in parts of Asia they are a delicacy, with a nutty flavour; Santa Monica Mountains rangers warned of bites in 2018; https://www.kqed.org/science/1979474/dont-go-chasing-water-bugs

beats.say: This bug can eat a turtle. It melts the insides, and drinks them.
So I shrank myself down to its size, to get a closer look.
The giant water bug. Up to four inches long.
It's the biggest true bug in the United States and Canada.
It hides underwater, and grabs prey with its powerful legs.
Then it stabs with a dagger-like beak, and injects venom.
The venom turns the insides to soup. Then it sucks them out.
And the prey is probably still alive while it's being eaten.
And I complain when my soup is too hot.
It eats snakes, turtles, even ducklings.
Its nickname? The toe biter. Its bite is one of the most painful of any insect.
It also flies to lights at night. So some people call it the electric light bug.
In some kinds, mom glues her eggs onto dad's back. Then she leaves.
Dad carries them for weeks, until they hatch.
And in parts of Asia, people eat it. Some say it tastes nutty.
It drinks turtles, bites toes, and dad does all the babysitting.
Follow me. Next, an animal that can hit you with its spray from ten feet away.
